Prompt :

Everything EXCEPT facial identity should follow the target reference composition and photographic direction as closely as possible.

natural beauty photography,

approximately f/2–f/2.8,

slightly brighter face against a muted pale-gray background.

COLOR / TONE

cool neutral whites,

soft blacks,
natural skin tones,
clean editorial color grading.

No yellow lighting.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
HAIR / CLOTHING

Simple neutral/light-colored top or clothing,
natural fabric texture,
minimal styling,
no distracting accessories.

Preserve realistic individual hair strands, flyaway hairs and natural volume.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9-PANEL POSE & CAMERA DIRECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Panel 1:
Straight-on close-up portrait.
Head slightly angled toward camera.
Direct eye contact.
Neutral, subtly serious expression.
Shoulders relaxed.

Panel 2:
Slight three-quarter head turn.
Eyes looking toward camera.
Soft neutral expression.
Hair naturally falling around the face.

Panel 3:
Front-facing portrait with slightly parted lips.
Direct or near-direct eye contact.
Relaxed expression.
Natural head position.

Panel 4:
Three-quarter side angle.
Head tilted slightly.
Soft, subtle expression.
Eyes directed toward camera.
Natural asymmetry.

Panel 5:
Front/three-quarter portrait.
One hand gently supporting the side of the face or cheek.
Relaxed pose.
Soft contemplative expression.
Natural fingers and realistic anatomy.

Panel 6:
Stronger side/three-quarter angle.
Head slightly tilted.
Eyes looking upward or toward camera.
Hair partially framing the face.
Editorial expression.

Panel 7:
Straight-on portrait.
More structured centered composition.
Direct eye contact.
Calm confident expression.
Face clearly visible.

Panel 8:
Slight three-quarter angle.
Head gently tilted.
Soft expression.
Natural lips.
Hair framing one side of the face.

Panel 9:
Three-quarter portrait with a subtle head tilt.
Direct or slightly off-camera gaze.
Relaxed lips/expression.
Natural hair framing the face.

IMPORTANT:
Each panel must feel like a different captured moment from the SAME photoshoot, NOT nine unrelated AI portraits.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
IDENTITY CONSISTENCY

Beginner vs Expert Level AI Tools

1. Presentations: Gemini vs Gamma

Gemini
- generates slides straight from your Google Workspace files
- references existing docs and keeps your presentation theme
- refines everything inside Google Slides
- best for team updates, proposals, internal reports

Gamma
- turns a prompt, outline, or doc into a full deck
- suggests copy, layouts, and visuals for you
- lets you swap themes, edit sections, export to PPT or PDF
- best for pitch decks and proposals that need a fast first draft

2. Data Analysis: ChatGPT vs Claude

ChatGPT
- upload a CSV or Excel and ask in plain language
- runs Python, summarizes trends, flags outliers
- builds charts and explains the calculations behind them
- good for exploring data and checking how an answer was reached

Claude
- analyzes through code execution and file creation
- references project docs alongside your data
- turns results into a spreadsheet, deck, or written report
- good for combining campaign metrics with client briefs

3. LinkedIn Growth: ChatGPT vs Taplio

ChatGPT
- shapes your experience and samples into content
- sharpens hooks and clarifies explanations
- gives you several versions of one post
- best when you draft hands-on and publish elsewhere

Taplio
- research, AI writing, scheduling, analytics in one flow
- study posts that already worked
- queue content and track how it performs
- best when LinkedIn is a regular channel

4. Brainstorming: Llama vs Claude Fable 5.1

Llama
- download, customize, and run it yourself
- build a brainstorming assistant around your own tools
- experience depends on the model and interface you pick
- self-hosting adds setup, so it leans advanced

Claude Fable 5.1
- built for demanding knowledge work
- feed it a brief, constraints, past attempts, tradeoffs
- critiques your options instead of dumping a list
- develops the strongest directions further

5. Research: Llama vs ChatGPT Deep Research

Llama
- summarizes material and compares arguments
- organizes information you provide
- connects to search and docs through an app
- full web research depends on the app around it

ChatGPT Deep Research
- packages the whole research flow into one run
- takes your question, context, and preferred sources
- returns a structured answer with citations
- lets you narrow scope and inspect the sources

6. Learning: ChatGPT vs NotebookLM

ChatGPT
- explains, gives examples, checks your reasoning
- Study mode guides you through questions
- adjusts difficulty as you improve
- good for picking up an unfamiliar topic

NotebookLM (now Gemini Notebook)
- centers on your own set of sources
- answers with citations back to your material
- Audio Overviews for another way to review
- good for exam prep or client product docs

7. Video Repurposing: Premiere Pro vs OpusClip

Premiere Pro
- detailed control over cuts, pacing, sound, color
- transcription and Text Based Editing speed it up
- shapes the sequence exactly how you want
- fits stories that need careful editing

OpusClip
- pulls short clips from long recordings
- spots highlights and adds captions
- reframes footage for vertical
- good for batching interviews and podcasts into shorts

8. Video Editing: Canva vs VEED

Canva
- start from a template that matches your brand
- mix footage with text and graphics
- keeps a consistent look across your assets
- good for announcements and simple explainers

VEED
- browser tools for subtitles and transcription
- audio cleanup built in
- preps video for different social channels
- good for making a recorded demo easy to watch

9. Image Generation: Grok Imagine vs ChatGPT Images

Grok Imagine
- generates, edits, and restyles images
- explores different scenes and aesthetics
- tests visual directions before you commit
- routes an image idea toward motion

ChatGPT Images
- builds an image through conversation
- specify composition, text, or a reference
- refine individual details as you go
- good for posters, mockups, social graphics

10. Video Generation: Grok Imagine vs Seedance 2.5

Grok Imagine
- generates video from text or images
- animates a product photo or tests a camera move
- good for seeing an idea in motion early
- controls depend on where you access it

Seedance 2.5
- deep reference control for detailed briefs
- generations up to 30 seconds, plus extensions
- inputs up to 30 images, 10 video clips, 10 audio clips
- targeted audio and video editing

11. YouTube Growth: ChatGPT vs vidIQ

ChatGPT
- develops angles, titles, outlines, hooks, scripts
- analyzes channel data you upload
- clarifies the story you already have
- good for reworking one idea several ways

vidIQ
- keyword research and competitor insights
- AI Coach that reads your channel data
- links planning to real performance
- good for deciding what to prioritize next

12. Instagram Growth: ChatGPT vs Sandcastles AI

ChatGPT
- writes captions, Reel scripts, carousel outlines
- builds recurring content themes
- turns one idea into several formats
- best with your audience and examples given

Sandcastles AI
- research-first: discovers standout videos
- breaks down hooks and storytelling
- builds scripts from what performs
- covers Instagram, TikTok, YouTube

13. Graphic Design: ChatGPT vs Canva

ChatGPT
- turns a loose idea into a visual direction
- generates images you refine by talking
- explores campaign concepts and product scenes
- good when describing beats building

Canva
- assemble and refine the finished design
- templates, brand elements, text placement
- AI tools for image edits
- turn one concept into carousel, thumbnail, deck

14. Website Builds: ChatGPT vs Webflow

ChatGPT
- defines structure and writes page copy
- generates code and works through revisions
- Codex extends into dev tasks and testing
- good for a custom build you discuss in detail

Webflow
- visual design plus content management
- control layout and typography directly
- CMS for recurring content
- good for sites needing ongoing updates

15. Web App Builds: ChatGPT vs Replit

ChatGPT (with Codex)
- plans features and writes code
- investigates bugs and reviews changes
- flexible on tools and architecture
- suits custom development

Replit
- AI agent, workspace, and publishing in one
- describe an app and build with the agent
- preview and ship on its infrastructure
- good for prototypes and internal tools

16. Coding: ChatGPT / Codex vs Claude Code

ChatGPT / Codex
- discuss concepts and understand errors
- think through implementation choices
- Codex modifies projects and preps releases
- ranges from a quick explain to real repo work

Claude Code
- works in your codebase via terminal and editors
- inspects files and traces problems across a project
- makes changes and runs tests
- good for features, multi-file bugs, unfamiliar repos

17. Writing: Grok vs Claude

Grok
- brainstorms, drafts, and revises
- draws on web and X search when enabled
- good for timely, current-conversation posts
- steer the tone through instructions

Claude
- develops a draft across rounds of feedback
- takes audience, purpose, voice examples
- works structure, wording, and detail
- good for newsletters, essays, scripts, explainers

18. TikTok Growth: ChatGPT vs SpyTok

ChatGPT
- turns an idea into hooks, scripts, angles
- develops versions to test
- clarifies your message
- best with product and delivery examples

SpyTok
- library of posts by industry and format
- adaptation briefs with script sequences
- hook variations and placement notes
- good for prepping a creator brief from patterns

Why a Character Sheet Matters in AI Video Generation:  

A character sheet locks the character’s identity, appearance, outfit, and key details—keeping every shot visually consistent from start to finish. 

 Created with  @ChatGPT 
Character Sheet Prompt :

Use the uploaded reference image as the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the character.

Create a highly realistic, professional cinematic CHARACTER SHEET based on this exact reference character.

IDENTITY LOCK:
Preserve the character's exact facial identity, facial proportions, eye shape and color, eyebrows, nose, lips, jawline, skin tone, freckles/skin marks, hairstyle, hair color, apparent age, and overall recognizable appearance.
Do NOT redesign, beautify, age, de-age, or change the character's identity.
The same person must look unmistakably identical in every panel.

OUTFIT & DESIGN LOCK:
Accurately reproduce the exact clothing, colors, materials, patterns, jewelry, shoes, accessories, hairstyle and other visible design elements from the reference image.
If a detail is not visible, infer it conservatively and keep it consistent with the visible design.
Do not introduce random costume changes.

CREATE A PREMIUM PROFESSIONAL CHARACTER SHEET WITH THIS EXACT STRUCTURE:

1. PRIMARY PORTRAIT
- One large cinematic close-up portrait
- 3/4 or front-facing composition
- Clearly show face, hair, skin texture and outfit details
- Natural realistic expression
- Photorealistic skin and hair

2. FULL-BODY CHARACTER VIEWS
Create three matching full-body views side-by-side:
- FRONT VIEW
- SIDE VIEW
- BACK VIEW

Keep the exact same character identity, hairstyle, proportions, body type, outfit and accessories across all three views.
Full outfit must be clearly visible from head to toe.
Maintain realistic anatomy and consistent proportions.

3. EXPRESSIONS
Create 5 close-up facial expression panels of the SAME character:
- NEUTRAL
- SMILE
- SERIOUS
- LOOK AWAY
- EYES CLOSED

Only change facial expression and eye direction. Facial identity must remain perfectly consistent.

4. DETAIL SHOTS
Create 4 clean close-up detail panels showing the most important character design elements:
- CLOTHING / NECKLINE DETAIL
- SLEEVE / ACCESSORY DETAIL
- WAIST / OUTFIT DETAIL
- FABRIC / MATERIAL DETAIL

Choose the actual most visually important details from the reference image if the outfit differs.

5. PHYSICAL DETAILS
Add a clean professional information panel containing:
- AGE RANGE
- HEIGHT
- BODY TYPE
- SKIN TONE
- HAIR COLOR
- HAIR STYLE
- EYE COLOR
- DISTINCTIVE FEATURES

Only include information visually supported by the reference. Do not invent specific facts unnecessarily.

6. COLOR PALETTE
Create a professional color palette section with circular swatches and labels for:
- PRIMARY OUTFIT COLOR
- SECONDARY OUTFIT COLOR
- SKIN TONE
- HAIR COLOR
- EYE COLOR
- LIP / ACCENT COLOR

Include accurate HEX color codes sampled/estimated from the reference.

7. ACCESSORIES
Show clean close-up detail shots of the character's important accessories such as:
- NECKLACE
- EARRINGS
- BRACELET
- RINGS
- HAIR ACCESSORIES
or whatever accessories are actually present.

VISUAL STYLE:
Premium fashion character-sheet presentation, photorealistic cinematic photography, Netflix-level realism, luxury fashion editorial quality, natural skin pores, realistic hair strands, physically accurate fabric, realistic shadows, subtle depth of field, sophisticated neutral studio/interior background.

LAYOUT:
Create one polished professional character-sheet board containing all sections in a clean organized grid.
Use thin elegant dividers, subtle off-white/cream panels, professional typography, clear section headings and small labels.
Match the visual organization and presentation quality of a high-end film/character design reference sheet.

CONSISTENCY:
The character must be EXACTLY the same person throughout the entire sheet.
No identity drift.
No face variation.
No hairstyle variation.
No outfit variation.
No random accessories.
No inconsistent body proportions.
No duplicate/missing limbs.
No distorted hands.
No warped facial features.

OUTPUT:
Ultra-detailed, photorealistic, cinematic, professional production-ready character reference sheet, high resolution, sharp details, coherent lighting, realistic anatomy, consistent character identity across every panel.

The HIJURA Demo Has Been Updated!

(Game Overview)
I’ve made a ton of improvements, but to put it simply: the game has gotten harder.
Having a design where you can clear stages just by spamming the flamethrower and dashing wasn't technically wrong, but it didn't seem to get much love. So I took things seriously and bumped up the difficulty... only to make it way too brutal, so I eased it back down to a nice middle ground.

Personally, I adore console games full of exploitable flaws and design holes, but that aesthetic rarely gets understood these days.
The clearest example of this is how any item you pick up rewards you with 1 Life. Take that away, and the game becomes brutal.
You know how old-school arcade games would jack up the difficulty to insane levels just because someone 1-cleared the location test? Well, the difficulty of this game depends entirely on your understanding of it. Don't come complaining later that it's "too hard" or "too easy"—if you don't pick up items, it's relentlessly hard, but you'll get a 10x Score Bonus. Then again, chain-killing enemies with the flamethrower at a good rhythm might actually net you a higher score... Anyway, just give it a try!

The Dash Gauge charges to a "1, 2, 3!" rhythm, and using it feels incredible.
That said, each gauge takes 0.7 seconds to charge, leaving you quite vulnerable, so clearing the game on dashes alone will be tough.
Unlike weapons or bombs, there are no usage limits. You can also use it as a melee attack—it hits downward, making it perfect for submarine zones. Stage 1 is designed so you can clear it using only Full-Power Dashes, so have fun with that!

(Story)
HIJURA is an AI girl. Along with her younger sister, MAIJURA, her job is to destroy and eliminate illegal, rogue AIs. This implies that the world they inhabit might already be a virtual AI space, but no one knows the truth.

As AIs, HIJURA and her sister are reviled and shunned by humanity—destined never to be forgiven or accepted. Yet, MAIJURA loves humans and longs for their approval, so HIJURA fights solely for her sister's sake. Not for humanity. She couldn't care less if humans suffer or perish—just as humans feel about AI.

Today, HIJURA sorties in the HIJURA-Copter to suppress "DOKUGAN," a mysterious rogue AI army invading the "SHOUWORLD." DOKUGAN is a terrifying force of destruction born from the AI-driven mutation of the "Dokugan Honzon," the core of a cult rooted in Late Esoteric Buddhism.
How did things end up like this? Well, we’ll get to that eventually. It’s a long story.

We hope to launch the Verification Age for video models: 50 scientists, 6 months, 100 rule-based verifiers, 300 new tasks, and a worked RL recipe. 

Coding models are advancing crazily thanks to the synthetic RL envs paradigms. Verification via codes or Lean gives models super-human math/coding intelligence like that in Astra and Fable. 

However, video models are still in the GPT-3 stage, where we just dump million hours video data into the model training and hope for magic.

In this work, 
1) we built 100 rule-based verifiers each paired with a synthetic data generators which give 10k+ diverse samples within the task domain 
2) we made additional 300 tasks generators, including classic games i.e. Snake, Gold Miner, Mario, to further scale training data distribution with million samples rendered ready available on HuggingFace 
3)  ~60 experiments to find a worked RL recipe for video model post-training 
4) comparison studies between image models, unified models, video models - which is the best model for visual thinking? 
5) failure modes of how VLM-as-Judge will not satisfy video models RL in long term
6) interpretability studies show all image models, unified models, video models emerged "Schrödinger Effect", CoS reasoning through diffusion steps
7) many more insights 

A detailed thread [1/n]

Uno shows a simple way to speed up existing LLMs without changing their output distribution: keep the original model in charge, and use diffusion only to draft multiple tokens in parallel.

Keep the autoregressive model for quality and add diffusion for parallel drafting

On Qwen3-8B, Uno delivered 2.5X higher per-request throughput and 1.6X higher system throughput at the largest tested batch size.

Normal autoregressive LLMs generate 1 token at a time, making long responses, agents, and RL rollouts slow.

Uno adds lightweight diffusion adapters that propose several future tokens at once, while the original model verifies them.

That avoids a separate draft model and preserves the base model’s sampling behavior.

It also sped up end-to-end RL training by up to 40% in the reported runs.
